chunks: He means leucoderma (white spot disease). After some time, this disease afflicted Anas on his face, so he was not seen except with a veil.

key_terms.الرِّضَىٰ: Ar-Raḍī (a title/name, often referring to Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi or specifically here as cited by the commentator)
key_terms.الْبَرَص: Leucoderma (a skin disease causing white patches)
key_terms.مُبَرَّقَعًا: Wearing a veil/mask (to cover the face)

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'Baras' refer to in the context of Anas ibn Malik's illness in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: As-Sayyid ar-Raḍī clarifies that 'Baras' denotes leucoderma, noting that Anas ibn Mālik later afflicted by this condition on his face, which led him to wear a veil. This historical detail underscores the physical realities of the companions and the specific exegetical precision applied by Sharif al-Raḍī in interpreting the Amir al-Mu'minin's warnings. The mention of the veil highlights the social and personal impact of the ailment within the early Islamic community.

en.sayed-ali-raza: White spot means leucoderma. After sometime this disease did occur to Anas’s face so much so that he was never seen without a veil. [1]
